thought.text: Let me verify the rendered qgis command and then recreate the stack:

reasoning_content:
The QGIS command is currently in list format using `printf` (no heredoc issues) — the `$$` escaping renders as literal `$` at runtime. The nginx mount has been fixed. backend-wms has been added. Config validation OK.

Next is the tile server's mbtiles. Options:
1. Generate a minimal valid mbtiles so the tile server can start (documented procedure: user generates via Planetiler). A minimal empty mbtiles (just sqlite schema, no tiles) — tileserver-gl might accept it. Then the tile server starts up, and the style will return 200, but tiles may 404. That said, the tile server is just a nice-to-have for base map overlays.

Actually wait — I need to think about whether tileserver-gl will start with an empty mbtiles. "Not valid input file" was being output because the file didn't exist. With an empty (but valid sqlite) mbtiles, it should start. Tile requests to the germany source would return 404/empty. The light/dark style endpoints should return 200.

As an alternative, try to download real germany mbtiles — that would be a few hundred MB. Let me quickly check if there are known public mbtiles for Germany. There's "https://openmaptiles.org/downloads/germany/" — openmaptiles used to host germany mbtiles there (e.g., https://openmaptiles.org/downloads/germany/germany.pbf.tar.gz, ~700MB?). Those are openmaptiles styles, not vector tiles in the format this style expects. The style JSON (light.json/dark.json) references specific layers from the germany source. If the layers don't match, the map won't render properly. But the tile server itself will work.

Let me look at the README section on tile generation to check the expected format, and look at the style's layers.

Actually, the simplest, most robust approach: create a valid empty mbtiles with a schema matching what tileserver-gl expects (the standard mbtiles spec). tileserver-gl should start up without issues. The base map overlay won't display actual tiles, but that's the documented "user generates mbtiles" state — the repo intentionally doesn't include data.

Hmm, but is that enough to claim "installation success"? The documented access point for TileServer is https://tiles.localhost — that will respond (tilejson/style 200). The lack of actual tile data is an explicitly documented, user-generated optional data step (the README says "Setup Required: Generate mbtiles using Planetiler"). I think creating a minimal valid mbtiles (or leaving the tile server running with a warning) is acceptable, with a note.

Better idea: actually generate a small but real mbtiles using a tool available in the environment... Java isn't installed. Planetiler needs a lot of memory (Xmx8g, we only have 7.6GB) and ~1GB OSM PBF download. That's too heavy, and it's not required for the core installation either.

Decision: create a minimal valid mbtiles (sqlite with the standard schema) so that tileserver-gl can start and serve the style endpoint. Document that actual tile data requires the user to generate mbtiles with Planetiler (a documented step). This way the entire documented stack starts up.

So now:
1. Recreate the containers with the fixed compose (docker compose up -d) — this will create backend-wms and recreate nginx/qgis.
2. Create the minimal mbtiles.
3. Verify all services respond through Caddy.

Let me also double-check that the printf rendering of the QGIS command works. Let me quickly test the printf with sample values:
printf '[%s]\nhost=db\nport=5432\ndbname=%s\nuser=%s\npassword=%s\nsslmode=disable\n' qonnectra qonnectra qgis_user pass — the `\n` inside the format string is interpreted by printf. Good.

But note: in the compose list format `- |`, the literal text is passed as an argument to `sh -c`. The `$$` in the file renders to `$` at compose config time. At runtime, `$${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}` → `$QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra`? No wait — in the YAML list, the value is literally `"$${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}"`. Compose interpolates `$$` → `$`, giving `"$QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra"`? Hmm, no: the YAML text is `"$${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}"` — compose's env interpolation turns `$$` into a literal `$`, so the container command receives `"$QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra"`. Then at runtime sh expands `$QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra`?? That's wrong — the colon should be inside the `${...}` braces!

Wait, let me double-check: in the production docker-compose.yml, the printf line is:
printf '[%s]\nhost=db\nport=5432\ndbname=%s\nuser=%s\npassword=%s\nsslmode=disable\n' "$${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME}" "$${DB_NAME}" "$${QGIS_DB_USER}" "$${QGIS_DB_PASSWORD}"

So the production version uses `$$` without the `:-` default (the env var is passed to the container's environment, and compose's `${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}` default only applies at compose time, not at container runtime). In my dev version I used `$$` with `:-qonnectra` — compose interpolates `$$`→`$`, leaving `$${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}` → `$` + `${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}`. Let me re-check the actual YAML text I wrote:

`printf '[%s]\\nhost=db\\n...\\n' "$${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}" "$${DB_NAME}" ...`

In the YAML file: `"$${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}"`. Compose variable interpolation: `$$` → literal `$`. So the runtime string becomes: `"$QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra"`??

Hmm, no! The interpolation is done on the raw text: the text is `$${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}`. The interpolation engine scans for `$` followed by an identifier/brace. When it sees `$$`, it produces a literal `$` and continues scanning after those two characters. The next character is `{QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}` — that's not a valid variable reference (a `$` is needed before the brace). Since there's no `$` before the brace, it's left as a literal. So the runtime string = `$` + `{QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}` = `${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}`.

So at sh runtime: `"$QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra"` — no wait, it becomes the 6 characters `$` + `{...}` = `${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}`, which sh expands as a parameter expansion with a default. Correct!

Let me validate with `docker compose config` what the rendered command looks like.
